Era IX · The Scourge's Retaliation
Meanwhile, the Scourge villagers went about their own work.
They took no part in the beacon purification —
they were researching an art of resurrection of their own.
The Builders did not trust them; the Scourge villagers did not wish to ally with them.
They meant to prove it on their own:
that Scourge magic, too, could call back the dead.
They failed.
What their resurrection raised was not the living — it was the Undead.
Zombies, skeletons, husks —
these were the things the Undead Rot bred.
The Undead Rot was nothing like the Wither Blight —
the Wither Blight was "radiation harm"; the Undead Rot was dominion over the dead.
Those it took did not turn Withered; they became mindless puppets of the Undead.
The Scourge villagers' research had failed utterly.
The Undead they had raised turned back on them.
They watched the monsters they had summoned kill their own kin,
watched the circle yield not the risen, but the walking dead —
and they were seized with rage.
Not rage at others. Rage at themselves.
They felt cheated, backlashed by the power itself, mocked by their own "noble intentions".
From "Scourge villagers who dreamed of being heroes"
they became "Warlocks who wanted to destroy everything".
They began raiding villages, striking at the Builders, taking all they could.
That is why the Warlocks seem so mad today —
they once were good people trying to save the world.
